transcript.content:
A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: I'll start by listing the tables and their schemas.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, service_name, COUNT(*) n, AVG(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, SUM(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY service_name UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, COUNT(*), AVG(duration)/1e6, SUM(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM normal_traces GROUP BY service_name ORDER BY service_name, p
SELECT metric, service_name, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(value),2) avg_v, MIN(value) mn, MAX(value) mx FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY metric, service_name ORDER BY metric, service_name

content.text: Reservation and rate traffic dropped sharply in the incident period. Next I'll break down spans by name, kind and pod.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind k, attr_status_code sc, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, COUNT(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) pods FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, attr_status_code, COUNT(*), ROUND(AVG(duration)/1e6,2), COUNT(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: The main signal: `search` → `rate.Rate/GetRates` client spans fail almost instantly (1100 errors, about 0.01 ms), and `rate` server spans nearly vanish. I'll check rate's pods, metrics and logs, and the search→rate network connection.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, attr_source src, attr_destination dst, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(value),2) avg_v, MIN(value) mn, MAX(value) mx FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, attr_source, attr_destination, COUNT(*), ROUND(AVG(value),2), MIN(value), MAX(value) FROM normal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6 ORDER BY 2,3,4,1

content.text: Search's `GetRates` calls fail in about 10 µs, while rate's own server spans almost disappear. I'll look at search's error log messages to tell a DNS failure from a partition or refusal.

input.query: SELECT service_name, level, LEFT(message,300) msg, COUNT(*) n FROM abnormal_logs WHERE level IN ('ERROR','WARN') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 10

SELECT service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, attr_k8s_service_name ksvc, attr_status_code sc, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(duration)/1e6,3) avg_ms, MAX(duration)/1e6 max_ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 1,2

content.text: Search's failures are instant and rate receives almost no requests, so I need to determine whether the fault sits on rate's side or on search's side. Next I'll check pod uptime and restarts across all services.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(MIN(value),0) umin, ROUND(MAX(value),0) umax FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric='k8s.pod.uptime' GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, COUNT(*), ROUND(MIN(value),0), ROUND(MAX(value),0) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE metric='k8s.pod.uptime' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

SELECT 'ab' p, metric, COUNT(DISTINCT service_name) svcs, COUNT(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, COUNT(DISTINCT service_name), COUNT(*) FROM normal_metrics GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: Rate pods have no uptime, CPU or network rows in the abnormal period, but do have span-metric rows. I'll check rate's gauge metrics and the restart and ready counters.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, metric, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(value),2) av, ROUND(MIN(value),2) mn, ROUND(MAX(value),2) mx FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('rate','search','memcached-rate-1','mongodb-rate') OR metric IN ('k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.phase') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, metric, COUNT(*), ROUND(AVG(value),2), ROUND(MIN(value),2), ROUND(MAX(value),2) FROM normal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('rate','search','memcached-rate-1','mongodb-rate') OR metric IN ('k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.phase') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,3,4,1

content.text: The rate container crash-loops in the abnormal window: restarts climb from 2 to 6 and `ready` stays at 0, versus 0 restarts and ready=1 in normal. Next I'll confirm how the failure travels up through the trace trees.

input.query: WITH f AS (SELECT trace_id, span_id, span_name, attr_status_code FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='frontend' AND attr_span_kind='Server') SELECT f.span_name, f.attr_status_code fsc, c.service_name child_svc, c.span_name child_span, c.attr_status_code csc, COUNT(*) n FROM f JOIN abnormal_traces c ON c.trace_id=f.trace_id AND c.parent_span_id=f.span_id GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 ORDER BY 1,3,4
